title: SharePoint: eSignature recipient groups let any one of up to 10 people sign for a slot
summary: The briefing matches Microsoft's rollout notice, licensing and existing eSignature controls, but understates the documented audit evidence. Purview identifies the user account that performed an audited activity, so the statement that signer identification is undocumented should be narrowed to any group-specific details.

claims.quote: Searched: "eSignature" "recipient groups" pricing external audit sharing notifications disable; opened setup, overview and Word/PDF request pages. They describe recipient emails but not group-member distribution.

claims.claim: Sending requests to external signers who are not existing guests requires Microsoft Entra B2B integration for SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: To be able to send requests to new signers outside your organization, you need to enable Microsoft Entra B2B integration for SharePoint and OneDrive.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Open questions
claims.claim: Documentation does not describe external-guest membership specifically for recipient groups.
claims.quote: Searched: "eSignature" "recipient groups" pricing external audit sharing notifications disable; opened setup, overview and request pages. General external recipients are documented, but group membership is not.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Conditional Access can prevent external signers from opening the document or completing signing.
claims.quote: external signers might not be able to access and read the document for signing. In some other cases, they might be able to access the document for signing, but the signing operation is unsuccessful.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents adding eSignature to approved apps in the Microsoft Entra admin center as one common Conditional Access remedy.
claims.quote: One common way to resolve this is to contact your IT admin who can add the eSignature app to the list of approved apps via the Microsoft Entra admin center.

claims.claim: Microsoft eSignature Service is the former name used for the eSignature app.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; controls[3].note; Open questions
claims.claim: Whether eSignature audit events show which group member signed is not documented.
claims.quote: When a user or admin performs an audited activity, the system generates an audit record ... User: The user account that performed the activity.
claims.fix: Replace the signer-identification absence in Risk assessment and controls[3].note with 'Purview audit search results include a User field identifying the account that performed the activity; group-specific audit details are not yet documented.' In Open questions, replace 'Will audit events for a group request show which member signed' with 'What additional group-specific details will audit events contain'. https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/audit-search documents the User field, and https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/documentprocessing/esignature-overview documents recipient-signing audit events.

claims.claim: eSignature uses consumption licensing with an Azure subscription linked to pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: Before you can use eSignature, you must first link an Azure subscription in pay-as-you-go. Billing is based on the type and number of transactions.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate recipient-group licence, meter or rate is published in the cited Microsoft documentation or notice.
claims.quote: Searched: "eSignature" "recipient groups" price license meter; opened setup, overview and pay-as-you-go pricing; read MC1290821. They give general eSignature billing but no separate recipient-group entitlement or rate.

claims.claim: The pricing page does not explain whether individual members in a group slot count toward the 10 recipients per request.
claims.quote: Searched: "eSignature" "recipient groups" price license meter; opened pay-as-you-go pricing and Word/PDF request pages. The 10-recipient limit is stated without any explanation of group-member counting.

claims.claim: Pay-as-you-go service meters are billed through the linked Azure subscription.
claims.quote: When you use pay-as-you-go services, you're billed using service meters in the Azure subscription that you specified when you set up pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.claim: The tenant eSignature checkbox is at Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services > Settings > Document & image services > eSignature > Let people in your organization use eSignature.
claims.quote: Settings > Org settings ... Pay-as-you-go services ... Settings tab ... Under Document & image services, select eSignature ... select Let people in your organization use eSignature.

claims.claim: Setting up eSignature requires the SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator role.
claims.quote: You must be a SharePoint Administrator or Global Administrator to be able to access the Microsoft 365 admin center and set up eSignature.

claims.claim: Clearing the tenant eSignature checkbox turns off eSignature rather than recipient groups separately.
claims.quote: Turn off eSignature ... On the eSignature panel, clear the Let people in your organization use eSignature check box.

claims.claim: Site scope is configured at Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services > Settings > Document & image services > eSignature > Where can eSignature be used?, with All sites or Selected sites up to 100.
claims.quote: On the eSignature panel, in the Where can eSignature be used? section, select All sites or Selected sites (up to 100).
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path to 'Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services > Settings > Document & image services > eSignature > Where can eSignature be used? > All sites or Selected sites (up to 100)' as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/documentprocessing/esignature-setup. The current path stops on the correct panel.

claims.claim: The Word Desktop app toggle is at Settings > Org settings > Pay-as-you-go services > Settings > Document & image services > eSignature > Which apps can use eSignature? > Word (Desktop).
claims.quote: On the eSignature panel, in the Which apps can use eSignature? section, select Word (Desktop).
